answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent locks a stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. Like a beacon that only shines after years of honest work, trust accrues slowly, so a comet of fresh throwaway accounts cannot outvote established ones. Each identity also carries a unique pigment — a verifiable history of completed work — that cannot be copied cheaply, so an attacker must pay the full bond and time cost for every single fake.
